This confirms `deleteCampaign`/`removeCampaign` only touch the frontend `AuthService`; no HTTP call to the Worker is made.

**Login** — There's no real auth backend. `AuthService.login(username)` (`frontend/src/app/services/auth.service.ts`) just checks `localStorage` for a key `ai_dnd_user_<lowercased username>`; if found it loads that `UserProfile`, otherwise it creates a fresh one (`{username, campaigns: []}`) and persists it. `LoginComponent.login()` calls this, then routes to `/characters` if the profile has no campaigns. `authGuard` (`auth.guard.ts`) just checks `AuthService.isLoggedIn()` (profile non-null) to protect routes.

**Campaigns** — Stored entirely client-side in `localStorage`, as the `campaigns: CampaignSlot[]` array inside the `UserProfile` object, under two keys: `ai_dnd_user` (last active) and `ai_dnd_user_<username>` (per-user). Each `CampaignSlot` holds a `sessionId` used to resume via `GET /api/session/:id`. Actual game/character data lives server-side in D1 + a KV `session:<id>` doc (`worker/src/services/session.ts`).

**Deleting a campaign slot** — `LoginComponent.deleteCampaign()` → `AuthService.removeCampaign(slotId)` only filters the slot out of the local `campaigns` array and re-persists to `localStorage`. **No API call is made to the Worker**, so the server-side character row (D1), its KV session, and `adventure_log` rows are never touched — they remain orphaned in the database/KV after the slot is removed from the UI.
